questions.q: Pathology of pseudoexfoliation (PXF) glaucoma per p113:
opts: LOX-1 gene mutation → pseudoexfoliative material produced → deposited in different locations
Optineurin mutation → retinal ganglion cell loss
questions.exp: Pathology: LOX-1 gene mutation → pseudoexfoliative material produced → deposited in different locations. (Book p113)

questions.q: Locations of pseudoexfoliative deposits per p113 include all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Deposits at trabecular meshwork, pupillary margin, lens capsule, near Schwalbe's line, corneal endothelium — not optic disc. (Book p113)

questions.q: Match deposit location with feature/name per p113 — 1) Trabecular meshwork 2) Pupillary margin 3) Lens capsule 4) Near Schwalbe's line … A) Target sign B) Sampaolesi line C) m/c cause of 2° OAG, mostly unilateral D) Fnocks — poor mydriasis, difficulty during cataract Sx (ruled out pre-operatively)
questions.exp: TM: m/c cause of 2° OAG, mostly unilateral; pupillary margin: Fnocks, prevents pupillary dilatation (poor mydriasis) → difficulty during cataract Sx; lens capsule: target sign; near Schwalbe's line: Sampaolesi line. (Book p113)

questions.q: Which statement per p113 about PXF deposits is TRUE?
opts: Corneal endothelium shows the target sign
Lens capsule deposits give Krukenberg spindle
Pupillary margin deposits prevent pupillary dilatation (poor mydriasis)
questions.exp: Pupillary margin Fnocks prevent pupillary dilatation (poor mydriasis) → can cause difficulty during cataract Sx; TM deposits cause 2° OAG; lens capsule gives target sign. (Book p113)

questions.q: Target sign per p113 = pseudoexfoliative deposits on the ___ showing central clear zone, clear zone and peripheral zone.
questions.exp: Lens capsule → target sign: central clear zone, clear zone, peripheral zone with deposits. (Book p113)

questions.q: Pigmentary glaucoma per p113 is m/c in:
questions.exp: m/c in young male myopes. (Book p113)

questions.q: Match pigmentary deposit location with clinical feature per p113 — 1) Corneal endothelium 2) Trabecular meshwork 3) Ciliary zonules (insertion on lens) 4) Schwalbe's line … A) 2° OAG B) Zentmayer's line C) Sampaolesi line D) Krukenberg spindle
questions.exp: Corneal endothelium → Krukenberg spindle; TM → 2° OAG; ciliary zonules (insertion on lens) → Zentmayer's line; Schwalbe's line → Sampaolesi line. (Book p113)

questions.q: In both PXF and pigmentary glaucoma per p113, deposits near/at Schwalbe's line are called ___.
questions.exp: Near Schwalbe's line (PXF) and Schwalbe's line (pigmentary) → Sampaolesi line. (Book p113)

questions.q: Match lens induced glaucoma per p114 — 1) Phacomorphic 2) Phacolytic 3) Phacotopic … A) Microspherophakia: lax zonules → anterior lens displacement blocking pupil → 2° ACG B) Intumescent cataract: lens swelling contacts pupillary margin → blocks aqueous flow → 2° ACG C) Morgagnian cataract: liquefied lens proteins leak → block trabecular meshwork → 2° OAG
questions.exp: Phacomorphic = intumescent cataract → 2° ACG; phacolytic = Morgagnian, liquefied proteins block TM → 2° OAG; phacotopic = microspherophakia anterior displacement → 2° ACG. (Book p114)

questions.q: All describe phacolytic glaucoma per p114 EXCEPT:
opts: Liquefaction of lens proteins with fluid leak
questions.exp: Intumescent lens blocking the pupil = phacomorphic; phacolytic = Morgagnian with liquefied lens proteins leaking and blocking TM. (Book p114)

questions.q: Treatment of phacomorphic and phacolytic glaucoma per p114:
questions.exp: Both treated by cataract surgery. (Book p114)

questions.q: Phacotopic glaucoma mx per p114:
opts: Pilocarpine to constrict the pupil and pull the iris away from angle
IV mannitol alone as definitive therapy
Atropine ± peripheral laser iridotomy (dilates pupil, opens block)
questions.exp: Atropine dilates pupil → opens block; peripheral laser iridotomy. (Book p114)

questions.q: Microspherophakia per p114 is:
opts: Congenital small spherical lens with laxing of zonules and ↑ lens movement
questions.exp: Microspherophakia: congenital anomaly; small spherical lens → laxing of zonules → ↑ lens movement → anterior displacement blocks pupil → 2° ACG. (Book p114)

questions.q: Malignant glaucoma per p114 is known by all these names EXCEPT:
questions.exp: AKA ciliary block glaucoma / aqueous misdirection syndrome / inverse glaucoma — it is 2° ACG WITHOUT pupillary block. (Book p114)

questions.q: Etiology of malignant glaucoma per p114:
questions.exp: Etiology: incisional or laser surgeries. (Book p114)

questions.q: Pathogenesis of malignant glaucoma per p114:
opts: Iris neovascularization rubeosis blocking the angle
2° ACG with pupillary block and posterior synechiae
Primary trabecular degeneration with open angle and chronically high IOP
2° ACG without pupillary block; aqueous misdirected posteriorly
questions.exp: 2° ACG without pupillary block; anterior rotation of ciliary processes → aqueous produced posteriorly → ↑ pressure → iris lens diaphragm pushed forwards. (Book p114)

questions.q: Rx of malignant glaucoma per p114:
opts: Cycloplegic (eg atropine) → relaxes ciliary muscle → zonules stretched → lens pulled posteriorly → normal aqueous flow
Pilocarpine to constrict the pupil and open the angle
Miotics such as demecarium given long term
questions.exp: Rx: cycloplegic (eg atropine) → relaxes ciliary muscles → zonules stretched → lens pulled posteriorly → normal aqueous flow. (Book p114)

questions.q: Inverse glaucoma pair (ACG Rx by atropine instead of pilocarpine) per p114:
questions.exp: Note: phacotopic glaucoma and malignant glaucoma = inverse glaucoma (ACG Rx by atropine instead of pilocarpine). (Book p114)

questions.q: Days after uneventful trabeculectomy a patient shows shallow AC with raised IOP and no pupillary block per p114. Diagnosis and Rx:
questions.exp: Malignant (ciliary block/aqueous misdirection) glaucoma follows incisional/laser surgery; 2° ACG without pupillary block; Rx cycloplegic eg atropine. (Book p114)

questions.q: ICE syndrome per p115: primary abnormality is corneal endothelium giving ___ appearance of cornea.
questions.exp: Primary abnormality: corneal endothelium; silver hammer appearance of cornea. (Book p115)

questions.q: Associated finding in ICE syndrome per p115:
questions.exp: Associated finding: 2° ACG. (Book p115)

questions.q: Match ICE variants per p115 — 1) Progressive iris atrophy 2) Chandler syndrome 3) Cogan-Reese syndrome … A) Corneal edema B) Iris nevus (pigmented lesion on iris) C) Polycoria and corectopia
questions.exp: Progressive iris atrophy: polycoria (multiple pupils) + corectopia (abnormal pupil position); Chandler syndrome: corneal edema; Cogan-Reese syndrome: iris nevus. (Book p115)

questions.q: Primary congenital glaucoma onset m/c per p115:
questions.exp: Age of onset m/c <3 yrs (95%); no other associated disease. (Book p115)

questions.q: Mechanism of primary congenital glaucoma per p115:
questions.exp: Mechanism: trabeculodysgenesis (TM malformation) causes OAG. (Book p115)

questions.q: Symptom triad of congenital glaucoma per p115:
opts: Blepharospasm is the m/c symptom while photophobia is late
Lacrimation is the earliest symptom and blepharospasm m/c
Ocular pain is the earliest symptom of the triad
questions.exp: Triad: blepharospasm, photophobia (earliest symptom), lacrimation (m/c symptom). (Book p115)

questions.q: Corneal diameter in buphthalmos per p115:
questions.exp: Corneal diameter >13 mm (normal 10-11 mm in children); children's eyeball easily distends under pressure. (Book p115)

questions.q: Match congenital glaucoma signs per p115 — 1) Endothelial breaks 2) Horizontal breaks in Descemet's 3) Scleral stretching 4) Deep AC … A) Haab's striae visible against fundal glow B) Hazy cornea d/t aqueous entry C) Blue sclera d/t thinning with underlying vessels visible D) ↑ Axial length → axial myopia
questions.exp: Endothelial breaks → aqueous enters cornea → hazy cornea; horizontal breaks in Descemet's → Haab's striae (visible against fundal glow); scleral stretching → thinning → underlying vessels visible → blue sclera; deep AC → ↑ axial length → axial myopia. (Book p115)

questions.q: Gonioscopic findings in congenital glaucoma per p116 include all EXCEPT:
opts: Loch Ness monster phenomenon (loops of vessels visible)
questions.exp: Gonioscopic findings: anterior iris insertion, Barkan membrane, Loch Ness monster phenomenon (loops of vessels visible). (Book p116)

questions.q: Rx of choice for congenital glaucoma per p116:
questions.exp: Rx of choice combined procedure: trabeculectomy (cutting of some TM) + trabeculotomy (holes in remaining TM). (Book p116)

questions.q: Goniotomy per p116 can be performed if:
questions.exp: Goniotomy: needle piercing of TM using a gonioscope to visualize; can be performed if cornea is clear (if onset >2 yrs). (Book p116)

questions.q: Trabeculotomy per p116 is:
opts: Formation of holes in the remaining TM
questions.exp: Trabeculectomy = cutting of some TM; trabeculotomy = formation of holes in the remaining TM. (Book p116)

questions.q: Mechanism of secondary congenital/developmental glaucoma per p116:
questions.exp: Mechanism: irido trabeculo corneal dysgenesis. (Book p116)

questions.q: Causes of secondary congenital/developmental glaucoma per p116 include all EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Causes: Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome, Peter's anomaly, aniridia (ectopia lentis and glaucoma), phacomatosis (NF, Sturge Weber syndrome). (Book p116)

questions.q: Glaucoma in Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome per p116 occurs in:
questions.exp: Glaucoma in 50% cases. (Book p116)

questions.q: Posterior embryotoxon per p116:
questions.exp: Posterior embryotoxon: anteriorly displaced Schwalbe's line. (Book p116)

questions.q: Phacomatoses causing developmental glaucoma per p116:
questions.exp: Phacomatosis: NF, Sturge Weber syndrome. (Book p116)
